utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We shall now continue with the evidence of Professor Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... continue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you, too, Professor Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 6D1305 for the Serbian version and P1072 for the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have English version of P1072, so I kindly ask to have that English version on the left screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see it now. What are these rules like in relation to the police?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the basic rule book in view of the police, the rules on the internal organization of the Ministry of the Interior, that is to say that each and every ministry has a rule book of its own and these rules are passed by the government, adopted by the government within a term prescribed by the law. Within the field of the interior, the Ministry of the Interior, the minister adopted this and the Government of the Republic of Serbia adopted this within a certain procedure, and these rules constituted a basis for the internal organization and the work of the police. In addition to this rule book, there are other documents that support it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Article 7 now, please, paragraphs 1 and 2, page 9 in e-court in Serbian and in English page 10 in e-court. What can be seen from Article 7, Professor?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see the heading, what is set is the joint purview of the organizational units. So that is the title of the chapter. Article 7 deals with the organizational units within the ministry, primarily the two departments of public security and state security; and another thing that is referred to are the administrations that are within the seat of the ministry. This only has to do with public security, whereas state security has its own rule book which resembles this one to a large degree and there are some differences too in terms of organization. Article 7 shows that a department, or rather, the department of public security and the administrations within it are responsible for the situation for which they were established. So the crime police administration for crime matters, then the police administration for police matters, and so on and so forth. So these departments and administrations are responsible for their own line of work and they set the organizational process down the line of work within the ministry from the administration to a particular police station or police unit that on the ground carries out certain lawful activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I've been speaking too fast. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you said concerning unity or singleness was not included.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Departments and administrations within their lines of work ensure the unity of internal organizational and working processes within the entire system and the field for which the administration was established starting from the headquarters or seat all the way down to the last organizational unit at local level, or particular units, police units, that act on the basis of these rules. The essence of this is that this unity of the organizational and work process goes all the way down from the seat of the MUP downwards, that is, and it involves a series of activities and tasks that have to be carried out by the administration, like control, supervision, different levels of planning, and a series of activities that are prescribed in these articles and that constitute the essence of the internal process of work, which means that this article defines the interconnectedness and the unity of work of the administrations that are organized within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of this article and the other regulations, the staff of the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija, did it have authority to plan, organization, and be in charge of the work and organization of organizational units? Could something like that happen on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff had not been envisaged within the system, it was envisaged within a document that could not change the relations that are defined in these rules, not only in this article but in a series of other articles regulating the work of the administrations in the ministry as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at subparagraph 3 of this article now, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does it speak about, paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says on the basis of the tasks that are envisaged in the previous article, the administrations and departments, each in its own line of work, ensure the interrelatedness and coordination work of respective internal organizational units, these are organizational units in the headquarters, like administrations, divisions within them and so on, secretariats, these are organizational units out in the field, secretariats, there were 33 of them in all of Serbia and then in Kosovo there were seven of them. And within these secretariats there are departments of internal affairs, police stations, and some special police units. The point is that this should ensure the unity of all these systems and subsystems within legal regulations pertaining to the Ministry of the Interior in Serbia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this system is there scope for a body on the flanks that would deal only with seven secretariats? Is there a place for the MUP staff for an independent link-up of the seven secretariats within the system?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP staff is not mentioned in this document, so it is not part of the system, the system of responsibility, the system of control. So therefore, it could not carry out the task that it was -- that was given to it in the decision on establishing the task. The system of organization had to be changed on both sides, the one that has to be adopted by the government. It was mission impossible at the time, so the staff therefore could not carry out what it wanted to carry out, what was given to it as a task. The best law and organization are a science, and that is telling proof of that. Nothing can come to life, it is not part of the system. If it is a foreign body, it will not be able to carry out the functions that it is supposed to carry out. I think this is the biggest mistake made by those who planned the work of the staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Simonovic, you will need --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to try harder to speak for slowly; otherwise, things that you say will be missed and that will not be of assistance to anyone. I know you've declared your intention a number of times, but you really need to give effect to it, please. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need Article 12, in the Serbian version it's page 10 and in English it's page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does Article 12 of these rules refer to, please, Professor? Just take it slowly.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 12 says that secretariats of the interior, all 33 of them, carry out all tasks within the sphere of activity of the ministry as established in these rules and shall be responsible for the security situation in the area for which they had been established within the ministry and within the administrations within the ministry. So in subparagraph 2 of this article it says that secretariats of the interior organize the work and management of departments of the interior and police stations within these secretariats, and that they are responsible for the work and functioning of these organizational units within the secretariats, they are responsible precisely to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something about the position of the staff within the chain of the MUP, and that pertains to chapter 9 of your expert report. I would like to ask you what regulations established the basic lines of information and reporting between the basic and area organizational units within the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the system that is derived from these rules, instructions on information reporting were adopted. These instructions entail a system of reporting and information within the ministry. It is of interest to note that there is no mention of the MUP staff within these instructions. These instructions envisage different forms of information and their essence is based on the following. The chain of information moves upwards as far as secretariats are concerned information from internal organizational units within the secretariats, that is to say police stations, police departments, moving towards the secretariat, the chief of the secretariat, and then to the operations centre in the Ministry of the Interior. Now, what was done in terms of the implementation of this document? On the basis of my studies, I only came to the conclusion that the only thing that could function on the basis of this was that after these rules another document was adopted, the one that we looked at yesterday, that was included in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court Exhibit P1044.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go on, Professor.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I? So this document - this is the document that's in front of me right now - it defines organizational units that exist, that is to say secretariats, and within the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, within this document, within item 5, what is envisaged within the system -- I mean it's an amendment to these instructions on information and reporting. Secretariats of the interior in Pristina, Kosovska Mitrovica, Urosevac, Gnjilane, Djakovica, Pec, and Prizren, that is to say the secretariats in the territory of Kosovo, send dispatches at the same time to the ministry and the ministry staff in Pristina. That was indeed carried through, and it became part of the system and it did function. Any other request based on the decision to establish the staff would require a change of the system itself, but it's easier to change the system in the field of information than in the field of control responsibility because that requires a change of the overall system. Can I just put a question? Can this be interpreted, all of this that I've been saying now? Can you follow what it is that I've been saying -- very well. I have explain this if Their Honours wish me to do so, why this was included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's from 1996, I know that. It's 19th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's prior to any of these documents in relation to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. May I be allowed to say something, Your Honours? Instruction on information and reporting was enacted in December 1994, which means that this document is 1996, two years later, and it introduced into -- changes into the system of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now may we have the last page of that document, please, on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were telling us a moment ago about the upward trend, the SUP obligation to inform the staff, and this portion speaks of the downward line, from top to bottom issuing orders. So what can we see here if we look at paragraph 5 on that last page, and it is under Roman III?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at point 5 in the Roman III area it says the following: "When an organizational unit from the ministry main office," so the main office we're talking about now, and it is the administration of the crime police, for instance, the police administration or any other administration for that matter, "spends dispatches downwards, it addresses them in one of the following ways: Giving instructions under 1, SUP to all, 1 to 33," and then underneath that we have staff of the ministry of Pristina. So this is introduced as an auxiliary, secondary body to be informed on the flanks. And now number 2: "SUP, the secretariat, the police station," and so on and so forth, to all. So this part of the task could take effect because they were introduced into the actual system, and it indicates that, in fact, the staff of the ministry that is stipulated here underneath the SUP in that line, down that line - and you can see that visually on this document - is not just form but substance, a reflection of the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now let's go back for a moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just -- this is still the 1996 document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and it was in force at the material time, the time we're discussing now. All the documents that we studied in dealing with this subject matter were regulated in this way and titled this way, that is to say at the beginning of the document in the upper left-hand corner you -- the heading would show this because that's how the system was established with slight exceptions here and there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. So may I now have a look at the combined document on the e-court 6D1305 of the page numbers, or rather the first one - the second one is P1072 in the Serbian version -- it says here that both versions are the same, so on the Serbian is page 9 and the English is page 9 and we need to look at Article 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, what does Article 8 address of the rules governing internal organization and establishment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next page in English, it must be 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead, but just slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article, or rather, in paragraph 1 it states that within this unified process of work or integrated work process defined by the previous article, Article 7, the departments, the department of public security here, shall perform tasks relating to programming, organization, management or governance, and promotion or improvement of the work in the area of internal affairs as standardised in the entire ministry. So this is, in fact, an attempt as opposed to para 2; to be more precise, in defining this internal unity in the sense of organization and the work process as defined compared to the administrations and organizational units such as the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what does paragraph 2 tell us?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 says that within the ministry, within the departments within whose composition they are, for example, the crime police administration, shall be immediately involved and engaged in carrying out security and other tasks from the purview of the ministry on the territory of the republic where this engagement is deemed necessary for the complete and timely implementation of tasks. So this provides for the fact that in addition to the internal organization of management and leadership by the departments down towards the secretariats, the administrations within the departments themselves and their professionals can be immediately involved in the execution of certain tasks if security reasons demand it. May I go on to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, from the central office the man goes down into the field and manages there?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a crime professor, and I know when a serious crime is committed then from the administration of the crime department professionals are sent from the area of detection, crime detection, on site they are included in the operative work and the on-site investigation to uncover the unknown perpetrator or perpetrators. So they work directly together with the local professionals and experts, that is to say the employees of the ministry within the frameworks of the secretariat, to resolve certain security problems. And this model in Serbia always functioned in the past and still functions and it is linked down to the chain of command and management within the frameworks of the ministries, which means if the problem occurs, for example, in the traffic security area, if there's a serious railway accident or aeroplane accident, then the work of the -- workers of the ministry from the administration dealing with traffic security go on the spot in the field, and the same is applied if other crimes are concerned. They go down to help the uniformed policemen, down to the police station. So this is a system that functioned at that time but it is quite outside the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor, let's not expand the subject, let's look at P1593, we don't have to have it on e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps it's a translation issue. I don't understand what you've just said at the end of your answer. The last sentence has been translated as: "So this is a system that functioned at that time but it is quite outside the MUP staff." I didn't dream that it was within the MUP staff, but what prompted you to say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- well, I don't know whether I was clear enough, made myself clear enough. What I wanted to say is this, that the system existed always before the staffs were established, it still exists today and it is a system which within this internal organization linked to the departments and territorial units and so on, it's a system that exists inside. And the MUP staff had nothing, had no relations with the way in which this functioned in the sense that it did not act along this line of tasks and this was not provided for by the rules and the rule book. I'm not sure whether there was all translated properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which MUP staff are you referring to? I mean, if it's the whole of Serbia you're describing at the moment, are you talking about the MUP staff in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's like this. In Belgrade there is no MUP staff. What exists in Belgrade is the Ministry of the Interior. Within the frameworks of that ministry there are two departments; within each department you have administrations. So the staff MUP only existed at that time in Pristina, now the staff that we're referring to here. Am I being clearer now? So this Belgrade you have the MUP, the Ministry of the Interior, with its administrations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here that in Kosovo and Metohija there was General Obrad Stevanovic or Gvozden Gagic present. Now, where was their base in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the picture I'm looking at on my screen is probably not related to what you were saying, this is probably a mistake, but it doesn't matter. As a crime professor, which I am, there's no problem when Gagic is in Kosovo and I heard what he said over the internet, that he went to Kosovo, he was sent there by his administration, crime police administration, to perform certain tasks linked to the registry and introducing changes into how crimes were recorded because the electronic system was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the legal grounds for his stay in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about Obrad Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, which means that they had the right to become directly involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly speak one at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The MUP staff, could it have any influence on the work of the seat of the MUP and the administration when they were engaged directly in the field in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this system, the system that was established by this -- these rules, first of all, bearing in mind Articles 7 and 8, but other articles too which define the tasks, rights, and duties and authorisation of each individual administration, these are other articles that I'm referring to, they clearly define this system of direct engagement so that the MUP staff couldn't be included in this system because it wasn't provided for in the beginning, it was outside this system of management and leadership, and that is something, if you organize legal norms within the police force, you will find that that is indubitably so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we should return now to Article 12, para 1 and 2. It is page 10 in the Serbian and page 12 in the English. You've already talked about this article.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask for the Serbian version to be placed on e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us who organizes the work of the police station.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 12 of these rules within the frameworks of Sava 2 prescribes that the secretariats in conformity with provisions 7 to 11 of these rules dealing with united organization within the MUP and management and leadership, that is to say the secretariats organized on the basis of those articles, the work that is to be done and the management of the departments of the interior, and the police stations within the municipalities and shall be responsible for their work. That means that this article regulates this system of control and organization established within the MUP and it is brought down to the level of the secretariats and then further down from the secretariats towards the internal organizational units such as police stations, police departments, and so on, but based on exactly the same principles. And this can be seen in Articles 7 to 11. We were looking at Articles 10 and 11 earlier on, or rather, we dealt with Article 7, that's what we analysed. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. We now need to look at Article 9, paras 1 and 2, page 9 of the Serbian and 11 of the English. And we're now talk about defence planning which is chapter 8 of your report and in fact we're going to be dealing with chapters 8 and 9 mostly today. What does Article 9 provide for?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 9 of these rules provides for the following, that the departments -- that the basic tasks of the departments is that they shall be responsible for organizing some imminent war preparations; that is to say they carry out the regulations, but regulations in emergency situations, they inform the organs of the republic and cooperate with other organs and organizations, of course within the frameworks of the law. Now, when we deal with defence and speak of defence preparations -- are you able to follow me, Your Honours? Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We now need to look at page 14 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why do you ask that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He asked me that question all the time because he speaks too fast all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's not a problem for us, that's a problem for interpreters. And if things are omitted, then only you and your witness will be responsible for that, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But Article 9 is referred to briefly in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need Article 15 in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's also referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just want to clarify a few points. In Serbian it's 14 -- page 14, in English it's Article 14, now it's difference in between these two acts. In English we need Article 14 on page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, can you see Article 15?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see Article 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From that can we see which administration within the department was in charge of defence?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this we can clearly see that the question of the country's defence within the frameworks of the system of the Ministry of the Interior is given over to the police administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Article 14 in Serbian, Article 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the frameworks of this article we have prescribed the tasks, duties, and rights of the police administration which are manifold, but for what we're discussing here it is important to note -- I have page 12 in front of me now, paragraph 2 of that law and that is not quite right, it should be the next page bearing in mind the text that I'm looking at now in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No -- well, the English -- you have the page in English. You've got Article 14 in English, the last paragraph. Is that not what you're looking for? The department for defence matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English should be Article 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we've got the last paragraph. It's mentioned in the report, we know what it says. What is it you want to add to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to connect it with the paragraph 4-0, 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us conclude with this, Professor. This administration, does it draft plans?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This administration drafts a plan of the defence of the republic under the competency of the ministry and this is its exclusive task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at Article 40. In English -- actually, it is Article 39, this being page 44; in the Serbian it is Article 40, page 36. Professor, are plans made within the SUP, defence plans and who's responsible for those?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the framework of this article, the obligation to draft plans is sent downwards according -- following professional lines from the administration of the police to the secretariats and the departments of the police in the area of secretariats, which are tasked with conducting preparations for the defence of secretariats in case of an imminent threat of war. It is stated that a department within any secretariat needs to establish organization and manning strength in case of an imminent threat of danger within the framework of the secretariat, the organized security measures, et cetera, so the obligation is set downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Studying laws and bylaws, did you ever come across the MUP staff being a part of the defence system within the framework of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff was not part of the system of defence of preparations. If I may continue I would say that -- well, let's go back to the level of administrations. Within the administration of the police, departments are formed; within those departments, we have sections immediately tasked with defensive preparations. For example, in the penultimate paragraph of the article which defines the tasks and authorities of the police administration, it is stated that within the framework of departments for PJP units reserve forces should be formed, within the PJP units and the reserve forces. Within those departments, sections are formed. Under 1, section for PJP units; under 2, section for defensive preparations; under 3, section for the reserve force. And then within the framework of the departments of the police within secretariats, based on the systemization of job posts and the law on the systemization of job posts, what is foreseen is a job post for an officer tasked with these tasks, defence preparations, reserve forces, and the training of the police in the mentioned situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A question or two about the planning within the MUP, it is in the same chapter. Let us go to Article 61 of the rule book on internal organization of the MUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do, just to be clear. It's not obvious in the English that's on the screen, but where is the reference to PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the document I have which was in force at the time within the framework of the police administration --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor, we have Article 40 on the screen. Tell us what article refers to PJP, what article in your rules.

utterances.text: Under the section --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it's part of that penultimate paragraph.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a part of Article 15, Article 15, which regulates --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your Honour, I had in mind Article 15 of the rules --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Concerning defensive planning --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defensive planning --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 61.

utterances.text: What is foreseen by Article 15, why did you mention the PJP?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, thank you. Can we have Article 15 then on the screen, please, and are we talking about the English 15, Mr. Lukic, or did it bear a different number in the previous --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- in English it's 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 14 in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we saw it before, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I want now to go to the second-last paragraph of that in English, of Article 14 in English. It seems to be the third-last paragraph in the English. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that is what I was talking about. I was trying to say that within that administration there were sections --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Departments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- including such sections as the section for defence preparation, the section for the PJP units, and as part of the same section it is called the section for the PJP and reserve force, and we were talking about defence preparations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the section for special police units, or PJP, is that an organizational unit of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the department for the PJP and reserve forces is an internal organizational unit, which is a part of the police administration, as part of the headquarters and the public security sector. We have the basic organizational structures, each containing its own internal organizational units. This is one such internal organizational units. Perhaps I needn't go to the law which regulates that per se.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor Simonovic, let us move on to Article 61, it concerns planning. In the B/C/S it is 61; in the English it is 62, page 61. In the B/C/S Article 61, page 46.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title of the article -- all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please continue slowly.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the article -- in the title of Article 61 in chapter 7 it says the way of programming and planning of tasks within the framework of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, such a planning system is defined. Within that system it is prescribed that the ministry puts forth programmes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just stop there. Now, this is all set out in the report, Mr. Lukic. Is there some particular point that's to be made in addition to what's in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I just wanted to move to connect with the document P1239, so this was just an introductory --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we understand what Article 61 says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have P1239 on the screens.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on, Professor.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before us we have instructions on the organization, implementation of the law enforcement activities in the security sector. This is an amendment to the rules and it was in force during the material time. It regulates the way police tasks should be carried out in the security sector, which means at the level of police stations and lower. This instruction directs the police force to how they should conduct themselves at the basic territorial units, these being the municipal and town units in keeping with the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English we need page 10, in the B/C/S page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Explain to us briefly these paragraphs -- rather, articles, Articles 29, 30, and 31.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Articles 29, 30, and 31 fall under the title Roman numeral V, planning, organizing, guiding and controlling work in the sector. In this chapter we have the system of planning, organization, directing, and control of the work of the police described as part of the sector. It is stated for that part of activities the secretariats are tasked to execute them alongside the police stations. In paragraph 30 it says the -- the planning, organizing, guiding, and controlling of work in the sector shall be carried out at the level of secretariats. In the following paragraph it says the commander of the police station and/or traffic police station shall be responsible for those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 26 in the English it is the previous page and I believe in the English [as interpreted] it also begins on the previous page. Professor, Article 26.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have it in hard copy?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it on the screen now. Could we please see Article 26. In Article 6 it says: "In discharging his duties in the sector, the sector leader shall undertake the following," and what follows are the tasks. Task number 1: "Directly discharge work and tasks in the sector," meaning that he plans, organizes, and directs work, extends professional assistance, directly assigns tasks and controls the performance of duties by the policemen. It is at the lowest level, the sectoral level. Then under 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us stop you. We will not go into any other sub-articles. I would like to go to Article 8 at page 4 in the Serbian, page 3 in the English. What can we see in Article 8?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article 8 we can see that at the level of the sector integrated law enforcement work shall be ensured; the same is applied to the level of the ministry at the level of administrations and then secretariats. The integration of law enforcement work is the issue at hand, in particular the planning, guidance, coordination, and control responsibility of the discharge of duty. The entire planning system is defined from top to bottom per organizational units. In practice it means that the sector leader at the level of a police station, as you know within any given police station there are several sectors, that particular sector leader needs to coordinate and guide the work of his policemen having in mind the specific security-related issues on the one hand and on the other hand keeping in mind the principles forwarded to him by the MUP. Such plans are adopted by the police station commander. Then in turn, the police station commander's plans that have to do with the station itself are adopted by the chief of the secretariat. One needs to say another thing here. In addition to sector leaders as well as police station commanders adopting plans for the work of the uniformed police in the sector, within each sector there is an analyst, a person collecting information and analysing, putting together a uniform plan for the police station. The traffic police department makes their own plans per traffic police sectors. On the other hand, the crime police department or -- and other departments within the secretariat also create their own plans following the same principles. These are general principles received from the ministry, in keeping with the specific security-related issues, they in turn try to make their own operational plans to cover those. Based on those plans at the level of secretariats we have operational plans for that particular month or an annual plan. Such plans are then adopted by the ministry as a general rule. Then each of the professional line plans need to be adopted by the professional lines in the ministry itself. What does it mean? A plan drafted by a police station commander. In addition to the chief of the secretariat, it also needs to be received by the police administration. As for the department of the crime police in their plan, it has to be approved by the chief of the secretariat as well as the police -- crime police administration in Belgrade. This system has always existed and it contains no staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor, now I'd like to move on to the way in which organizational units are controlled. 6D1305 is the document we need in Serbian and P1074 in the English version. In English we need page 59, Article 56; and in the Serbian version page 45, Article 54. Professor, it's going to show up in English as well, but let's not waste any time. Here it is. We have Article 56 in the English version. Tell us, please, about Article 56 in the Serbian version, what does it prescribe?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within chapter 6, under the heading: Mode of management of organizational units, this defines the tasks that are included in the articles that follow. It prescribed the principles of management and control within the Ministry of the Interior. Within Article 56 it says: "Departments, "resor," shall be managed by chiefs of departments, "resor" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a question you need to ask about this, Mr. Lukic? It's set out in plain English in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simonovic, within the system of control within the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, was there a place for the MUP staff as an auxiliary body?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this task to be carried through, as far as control, management, is concerned, first and foremost the staff would have had to have been envisaged as an organizational units and it should have the powers of an organizational unit; number 2, it would have to be contained in Article 54, that's the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at Article 58 now. In the Serbian version page 46 and in English we need Article 59 on page 60. Do these rules envisage a system of managing organizational units?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these rules do envisage a system of managing organizational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do we see that in Article 58?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article 58 what is defined are the tasks of the chief of the secretariat. In this way the system of management or control was brought down to the secretariat level and further down. The chief of secretariat is the number one person in the secretariat within the area for which the secretariat was established in accordance with the Law on the Interior, that is the law on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't read.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you know why this is important? I have to explain. In accordance with the Law on The state Administration and this is internal organization relations within work and so on, it is important to see who is in charge of the secretariat. So this entire system of secretariats, not only from the point of view of police work, but from the point of view of property law relations, employment law relations, and so on, all of that is in the hands of the chief of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that level, is there place for a MUP staff in Kosovo for it to take part in some forms of control?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would have had to be prescribed by this rule book. The system would have had to be changed. I told you at the very outset, the system had to be changed at the level of parallel information, that is the way it had to be handled, that is the only thing that will could be carried through in practice, however, it was not possible here because the chief of secretariat is not responsible for his secretariat, for his employees, who, to the ministry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, there's a limit to the number of times you can say the same thing. The witness is now pointing out to you, he said it at the outset, he said it in his report, there's no room for a MUP staff in Kosovo within the structure --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In different areas, we have comment, we have reporting, we have planning, so we have to clarify all these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. But I can tell you that I'm much more interested at this stage in knowing what the whole purpose of the MUP staff for Kosovo was according to the witness, but no doubt eventually we'll get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor, were these regulations in force in Kosovo and Metohija at the given point in time?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the relationship between the staff and the PJP, that is the last section in chapter 8 and in chapter 9 of the report, dealing with the rules again. In the English version we need Article 14, page 13; and now we're moving on to Article 15 on page 13 in the Serbian, the one that we had to jump to from Article 40. I cannot see it -- I see it in English, though. Article 15, what administration does it deal with?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police administration regulating the uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1998 and 1999 who headed the police administration?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Obrad Stevanovic, that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We said that the police administration is in charge of uniformed police. Was the PJP part of that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, they were uniformed police and they were within the police administration, as is stated here in this article, where tasks in relation to that are spelled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This police administration, does it draft certain documents related to PJP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This police administration does create a series of documents that have to do with different aspects of PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right, it's all enumerated so --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yet you said in this administration has certain departments?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certain departments that are further subdivided into sections. We've already talked about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just one moment. You're referring to paragraphs 8 and 9 of the report. Now, I don't think I've got a chapter 9. Chapter 8 is the internal organization of the Ministry of the Interior. Is there another -- is it the chapter on the MUP staff that's number 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It could be my mistake. I'll check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second, maybe it's page 83. Yeah, it may be it's just not got a number, but on page 83 there is a section headed: "The Republic of Serbia Ministry of the Interior staff for the prevention of terrorism" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was left on the previous page, the number 9, only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you. Now, can I ask just one question on this. Did I not read somewhere that the PJP were not necessarily what we understand as police officers? They might be people working in the fire service and from other sections of the ministry? Or am I confusing your report with something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer? May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, Your Honour, you observed this correctly. In the decision on the establishment of PJP units and in the foundations for the establishment of PJP units, it is stated that when PJP units are being established, within them, if necessary, specialists can be involved from other lines of work in order to make it possible to have work carried out in a comprehensive manner. For example, policemen from the administration of the crime police can be attached to them; for example, those who are from the fire section or, say, the legal affairs department. The Belgrade PJP, since it was rather big, it had an inspector for legality within it, in order to ensure comprehensive functioning; and that is stated in the document on their establishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1507, please, could we see that now. This is a decision on the establishment of PJMs, or rather, PJPs later. Professor, who adopted this decision?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it was. This decision was adopted by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell us when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was adopted in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 1st of August, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 1st of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 what does it say? Who can use the PJP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article -- in paragraph 2, subparagraph 2 of this decision says that putting PJP on the ready, bringing them together, and engaging PJM in terms of carrying out tasks from subparagraph 1 of this paragraph shall be carried out in accordance with an order of the minister if the minister does provide authorisation for this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question, it overlapped with the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You overlapped, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does point 7 tell us? It's probably the next page in English and in Serbian. Yes. Tell us who commands the PJP.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it is. The PJP commander commands the PJP, as envisaged by the document on job specifications within the ministry. So there is a position entitled the commander of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. At what level?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level -- I am sorry. The level of assistant minister, it corresponds to the level of assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I again clarify something. The P1072, the English version of the rules, what is the year that that was adopted, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, that's where Article 15, or as it was then 14, appears?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, in the other version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Professor, in the previous rules was there the equivalent of Article 15 prior to 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not really understand your question. Could you please try to clarify it for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, rule number or Article 15 of the rules is the one you drew our attention to which dealt with the special police units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the copy we're working on is from 1994. Did that rule exist in an earlier set of rules? And the reason I'm asking you is that the document we're now looking at was adopted on the 1st of August, 1993, so it predates the rules that we are looking at. So I want to know what is the authority under which the PJP was established if it was not under Article 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's under Article 6 according to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that makes it an organizational unit, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Professor -- we need page 1 in both versions, the introductory part - and could you please explain to us whether the PJP is an organizational unit; and if so -- or rather, if not, why was Article 6 of the rules on internal organization applied?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent question. When speaking of organizational units within the Ministry of the Interior, the basic article is Article 6 of the law of the Ministry of the Interior, which envisages that the minister can organize, establish, organizational units, or rather, rules defining them. Within the rules in Articles 2 and further on the organizational units are defined within the Ministry of the Interior starting with administrations down to secretariats and further on. However, in Article 6 of the rules on the internal organization of the Ministry of the Interior, the possibility was left for establishing organizational units by a decision to be made by the minister, a ministerial decision, which was not envisaged within these secretariats and administrations and their internal organizational units. What is prescribed then is that it is only the minister who can, through his own decision, through an individual decision establish these -- these special units or organizational units that are not within this system. On the basis of this Article 6, the minister established anti-terrorist SAJ. What was it now -- what did it stand for? The special unit for anti-terrorist operations, yes, yes. Now, how can we conclude out of these units established by the minister which ones are organizational units and which ones are not? Well, we can come to that conclusion on the basis of the document on staffing in the Ministry of the Interior, which envisages the staffing of the SAJ with exact positions, the commander, the assistant commander, the number of members --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do slow down.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I repeat this? I do apologise once again. I really have to keep myself under control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying -- it's a much simpler question. If something's established under Article 6 is it essentially an organizational unit or can it be something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, basically, but that is the specific feature of legal analysis. You can have an organizational unit, it can be that or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But we've had -- you see, we've had witnesses in this case who have told us that the PJP were not an organizational unit of the MUP, and that's why I'm asking you the question as an expert.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no problem. I'll try and answer that question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it sounded like a problem, Mr. Simonovic. Just give me a simple answer, if you can. What's your opinion? Just tell me your opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this. When it comes to PJP, when we're dealing with PJP, that was not an organizational unit because in principle it rallied these people around and not in the staffing rules --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. In that case could it properly be established under Article 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the PJP -- I understand. Now, in view of that, that the PJP rallied people within the frameworks of the administration of the police department, the departments and sections were formed, but it's just that part within the ministry which was in charge of planning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there not a yes or no answer to that? I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should there be another article or is it a mistake that it's number 6?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this number 6 can lead to misunderstanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me complete my questioning. It's quite inappropriate for that sort of prompting to come. I'm trying to establish directly with the witness what his opinion is about whether the PJP is an organizational unit, and he's now told me it's not. I thought a little while ago he told me it was, but I need to check the transcript for that. Now, what I'm really trying to establish is whether Article 15 of the 1994 rules was actually introduced afterwards to rectify a situation which had been created by this document, P1507. Is that what it looks like, Mr. Simonovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I'm absolutely certain that those rules were in force at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in that case no doubt you can make appropriate researches at a break and clarify the position for us later. Let's continue with Mr. Lukic's examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we were discussing the establishment of the PJP, I think that we also discussed whether it could be established pursuant to Article 6 or not. Was there any happier solution except for it be established pursuant to Article 6 in your opinion? We don't say it was a mistake; we're just asking whether there could have been a happier solution.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether we understand each other and I wouldn't like to speak off the top of my head, so that's the problem I'm having just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Never mind, let's move on. In this document let us look at points 4 and 5. Who could have determined the composition and the way in which PJP members were recruited?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this: The PJP was replenished or recruited by people from the uniformed composition within the frameworks of the secretariat. The principle for recruitment of the PJP was that within the frameworks of the secretariat lists of units were compiled in -- which included policemen who were regularly employed and the reserve police force, and the PJP units were formed within the frameworks of the secretariat based on the principle -- well, that means on the basis of this list, establishment list. And then we had units where members were rallied, not like the SAJ or JSO. So all the legal authorisations for policemen included in PJP units were realized within the frameworks of the secretariat, within the frameworks of which they realized their working status; and that is why these PJP detachments were not organizational units because if, for example, a policeman would carry out a misdemeanour, he would be held responsible to his secretariat because he drew up his labour relations within the frameworks of the secretariat and not PJP, as opposed to people in the SAJ who concluded their labour relations within the SAJ and was responsible to the commission and command of the SAJ. And that is the basic distinction based on this Article 6, that is to say units who had the character of organizational units and others which did not, and I think that is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now take a look at the next page in both the English and Serbian versions. We need to look at point 7. As I said, let's look at point 7 which we can see on our screens which states who commands the engagement composition. Well, anyway, who prescribes all this? Who is it who prescribes all this? Who has the authority to prescribe this?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was prescribed by the minister; he enacted or compiled this document. And how the document was to be acted upon. So the minister or the person that he designated, a person designated by the minister, and in principle the chain of command was from the commander of the PJP and we said that the PJP commander, the position of the PJP commander was established by an act on the staffing specifications of jobs within the ministry. Therefore, the chain of command goes from the minister through the head of the department to the command of the PJP as staffing commanders dictated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we need 6D411 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold this document for a moment. The members of the PJP were paid extra when required to act; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from this document and also from the basic premises on the establishment of PJP, which is the next document, we can see that they had some coefficient, some additional, additional sum to their salary, and it says -- it stipulates what that coefficient was. It was -- it's on the last page, in fact, found on the last page of document 6D411 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who paid it to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that payment went through the personal incomes paid out at the level of the ministry as a whole. Nobody else could have paid them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but were they paid by their own SUP or were they paid in some other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm quite certain in what I'm going to tell you next. The police at that time in Serbia and today was strictly hierarchically structured. Therefore, bearing in mind that hierarchy I'm sure that it wasn't the SUP that paid them, but it came from the MUP, a higher instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who paid them their regular salary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the same thing, they all received money from the MUP, the MUP paid them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's move on to 6D411, please, and we see that we have a document before us entitled: "Basic principles for forming special police units of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia." The date is the same as on the previous document, and it is the 1st of August, 1993, and we need to look at page 3 under V, control and command. Can you see that, Professor? And I'd like to ask you something in that regard. Who is it who can mobilise PJP units, who has the authority to do that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this article it specifically says or it gives an explanation that the recruitment of PJP can only be ordered by the minister of the interior or an official authorised by him, and then it says a special PJP unit shall be commanded by the commander through commanders of detachments and officers of lower establishment units. I apologise for being so fast. So let me repeat. Sentence 2 says: "The PJP units shall be commanded by the PJP commander," that is to say the work established within the systemizational staffing specifications through commanders of detachments and officers --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the PJP commander cannot mobilise the PJP himself; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he would need an initial act prescribing that from the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's just see -- not to go into e-court. Who orders the mobilisation of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mobilisation of the reserve police force is determined by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As reference 6D132, point 2. We don't have to have it up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the implementation of mobilisation, let that be recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you found it in the documents, acts, bylaws, and so on, that the PJP was commanded by the staff or chief -- the chief person of the staff or in the MUP of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this normative system that we're discussing now and organisationally speaking, it's quite clear that the chain of command is definitely defined, conditionally speaking the chain of command. In this chain the staff of the MUP for Kosovo is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time the staff was in existence, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to go on and ask you something else about the relationship between the staff and the SAJ. Once again it is to be found in chapters 8 and 9. We need 6D1355 to be called up on e-court, and we're going to add to that, or rather, we're going to add confusion -- the confusion surrounding Article 6 because you see here that it is on the basis of the same document and the same article that the SAJ was established just like the PJP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with an essential difference which provides me with the answer to your question, and that is this. May I go on? May I continue? If in the first document -- well, the document we were discussing a moment ago, we were looking at a moment ago, special decision on the establishment of special PJP units refers to Article 6 on internal organization, whereas the decision to establish and determine the SAJ refers to Article 6, para 2 of the Law on Internal Affairs which defines the organizational units. So that article of the law governing internal affairs gives the minister the authorisation to pass a decision to form organizational units in addition to those stipulated in para 1. And only then we come to Article 6, para 1 of the Law on Internal Organization. So that is an essential point which, as far as I'm concerned, express -- explains the difference between the legal status of the SAJ and the PJP units in addition to what we've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who passed this decision?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was passed by the minister of the interior, just like the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did the SAJ have a commander and deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the SAJ also had a commander, deputy commander, and that structure well the SAJ was an organizational unit, that is to say a member of the Ministry of the Interior would conclude a contract on employment in the SAJ but he could not do the same for the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to ask you something about the role of the staff in relation to the status and sanctioning of policemen, and linked to the status -- linked to status. The staff of the MUP of Pristina, or rather, before that let me ask you something else or linked to the SAJ. Did you find that the staff of the MUP of Pristina commanded and managed and led the special anti-terrorist unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff of the MUP in Pristina was not able to control the special anti-terrorist unit because, first of all, SAJ was an organizational unit, that's the first point, there was no staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But now we've gone back to the SAJ -- what was SAJ linked to directly?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SAJ was linked to the minister, linked up to the minister, or rather, the public section or department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now can we have a look at the first page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, SAJ was linked to the public security department, not to the administration, directly to the department, not the police administration. Its line, the chain, went from the chief of the department, which can be seen in para 1 of this document onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document has not been translated, so would you read out point 1 for us, please, but slowly.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Special anti-terrorist units are formed as separate units within the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia (the SAJ with its seat in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina)," which means that the SAJ was a unified organization with its respective parts in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina, they all comprised one unit, one whole, falling under the same command, regulated by the same act.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to the role of the staff in relation to the status and disciplining of policemen. The MUP staff in Pristina, did it have the authority to engage policemen in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorisation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you're responding we will need to have a look at P1737.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV SIMONOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorisation to deploy policemen was held by the minister or another official authorised by him pursuant to Article 72 of the Law on Interior. That law, in its Article 72, prescribes a possibility --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English it's page 21.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It envisaged a possibility to send ministry workers to other organizational units even if it was against their consent, if required by the security situation. I have that in front of me. The Ministry of the Interior can send, et cetera. The essence is that it has a direct link to the law on the state officials' work. That law empowers the officials of the ministry to be able to deploy workers of the ministry to other organizational units of the ministry without their consent for a period ranging between one month to -- up to a whole year. That was the legal basis, to introduce Article 72 as part of the Law on the Interior. And then pursuant to that article, certain employees of the Ministry of the Interior were sent to perform tasks in Kosovo. However, Article 72 does not refer to the members of the PJP because they were deployed according to the establishment lists following a different legal reasoning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the authority for assigning employees of organizational units -- well, what is an employee of an organizational unit? Does that include the chief of the department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does the term "employee of organizational unit" include the chief and the deputy chief of any administration or department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The answer is defined by the law. Legally speaking we can distinguish elected officials in ministries, according to the constitution, the assembly could elect the minister, the prime minister, and ministers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... General Lukic was - what was he? - the deputy chief of the SUP in Belgrade before he was in Kosovo. Now, was he an employee of an organizational unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His status was that of an employee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the authority of sending him to work in something that is not an organizational unit in another part of the territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was sent based -- well, in the decision I saw it says pursuant to Article 72 of the Law on Internal Affairs, that was the legal basis when the minister enacted that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is that wrong then? There's no -- that is not a proper legal foundation; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the legal basis seems to be fine. Under the law it is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what was the other organizational unit he was being sent to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have to refer to Article 72, excuse me. Let us see what the law says. Article 72 states: "The minister of the interior may assign employees of organizational units to perform official duties in certain organizational units in other parts of the territory of the republic until posts in such organizational units have been filled." I understand your question. Yes, that was a mistake. When I say "a mistake," it means that the MUP staff was not defined as an organizational unit; however, there was no other legal basis. Let us have a look at Article 16 of the Law on Labour Relations in state bodies and what it says. Your Honour, Article 16 of the Law on Labour Relations, should I wait for it to be shown on the screen or should I read it out loud in order to save time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just tell us what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Article 16 of the law it says, this is the Law on Labour Relations and State Bodies, it is the basic law for this regulation. "Employees of state bodies can be sent to other state bodies without their consent due to an increased volume of work if the officials heading those organs agree on such a transfer." Item 3 is interesting. The employee mentioned in item 1 of this article can exercise his or her rights and duties pertaining to labour relations with the initial organ, and thus you are correct. It was a mistake because the MUP staff was not an organizational unit, not a state body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's one way of looking at it. What you've just identified compounds the problem because if there is a proper legal way of sending Mr. Lukic to serve in a non-organizational unit and it's not used and the presumption in law would be that everything in an administration is done properly, then that would suggest that he was being sent to an organizational unit.
